We help businesses assess their arrangements, develop an appropriate methodology and prepare documentation that connects the analysis with the financial results — so the pricing position can be explained, evidenced and maintained year after year.

Advance Pricing Agreements and MAP support

capabilities.title: Economic Benchmarking & Comparable Searches
capabilities.description: Utilizing specialized global financial databases (Moody's, TP Catalyst, Orbis) to identify statistically robust comparable uncontrolled transactions across EMEA and APAC.

capabilities.title: Local File & Master File Architecture
capabilities.description: Drafting standardized, audit-ready compliance packages that reflect the value creation, DEMPE functions for intangibles, and commercial substance of your UAE entity.

capabilities.title: Intercompany Financial Transactions
capabilities.description: Assessing arm's length interest rates, credit rating methodologies, cash pooling arrangements, and financial guarantees in accordance with OECD Chapter X guidance.

capabilities.title: Advance Pricing Agreements (APAs)
capabilities.description: Direct negotiation of unilateral and bilateral APAs with the UAE Federal Tax Authority and overseas treaty partners to secure certainty for high-value transactions.

approach.title: Value Chain Diagnostic

approach.title: Economic Formulation

approach.title: Operational Integration

approach.title: Continuous Governance
approach.description: Annual monitoring, margin adjustments, and proactive audit readiness files.

whyItMatters.headline: Why Transfer Pricing Demands Specialized Advisory Today

points.title: FTA Audit Trigger
points.text: Intercompany management fees, royalties, and related-party financing are the primary focus of initial FTA audit inquiries.

points.title: Pillar Two Nexus
points.text: Pillar Two transitional CbCR safe harbors directly depend on Qualified Financial Statements and defensible TP allocations.

points.title: Penalty Insulation
points.text: Maintaining contemporaneous documentation is the statutory requirement to mitigate non-compliance penalties.

lede: Related-party transactions need a pricing approach that reflects the activities performed, risks assumed and commercial terms. We help businesses assess their arrangements, develop an appropriate methodology and prepare documentation that connects the analysis with the financial results — so the pricing position can be explained, evidenced and maintained year after year.
overviewDescription: Benchmarking, documentation and pricing policies for related-party transactions.
whenToInvolve: You transact with group companies, shareholders or other connected persons and need to evidence arm's-length pricing.
Your documentation, agreements and actual results no longer tell the same story.
You are restructuring operations, launching an intercompany charge or funding a group entity.
A tax authority has questioned a related-party transaction, method or margin.

subservices.title: Transfer Pricing impact assessment
subservices.description: We map related parties, connected persons and relevant transactions, assess the applicable obligations and identify information gaps. The assessment sets priorities for pricing analysis, documentation and changes to the way transactions are recorded or managed.
subservices.inPractice: In practice, this means working through your group structure, trial balances, intercompany invoices and contracts to build a complete inventory of controlled transactions — sales, services, royalties, loans, cost recharges and management fees. Each transaction is classified, sized and matched to the obligations that apply to it, so you know exactly what needs benchmarking, what needs documenting and in which order.
subservices.youReceive: A transaction-by-transaction inventory with a prioritised action plan and information-gap register.

subservices.title: Transfer Pricing benchmarking analysis
subservices.description: We evaluate suitable methods and search for comparable independent companies or transactions. The work includes functional screening, financial analysis and adjustments where supportable, with a clear explanation of the selected evidence. Comparable selection is based on comparability, not a desired margin.
subservices.inPractice: The search itself is documented step by step: database screening strategy, quantitative filters, manual review decisions and the reasons individual companies were accepted or rejected. We then compute the arm's-length range from the accepted set, apply working-capital or other adjustments only where they can be defended, and explain how your tested party's result compares.
subservices.youReceive: A benchmarking report with search strategy, accept/reject matrix, financial analysis and the resulting arm's-length range.

subservices.title: Transfer Pricing health check
subservices.description: We review existing policies, agreements, reports and actual results for inconsistencies. Particular attention is given to whether the documented arrangement matches conduct, whether charges are supported and whether the financial analysis can be reconciled to the records.
subservices.inPractice: We read your existing files the way a reviewer would: does the functional analysis match what people actually do, are the agreements signed and current, do booked margins fall inside the documented range, and can every intercompany charge be traced to evidence of delivery and benefit? Findings are graded by exposure so remediation effort goes where it matters.
subservices.youReceive: A findings report with issues graded by significance and a practical remediation plan.

subservices.title: Transfer Pricing Local File
subservices.description: We prepare an entity-focused account of the business and its material controlled transactions. The work connects the functional analysis, method selection, economic analysis and financial information, with supporting schedules that allow the position to be followed and reviewed.
subservices.inPractice: We interview the people who run the business, document functions, assets and risks for each transaction category, justify the method chosen and tie the economic analysis back to the statutory accounts. The file is written so a reviewer can move from the business description to the numbers without gaps, and it is structured for efficient annual updating.
subservices.youReceive: A complete Local File with functional analysis, method selection, economic analysis and reconciliation schedules.

subservices.title: Transfer Pricing Master File
subservices.description: We help assemble the group-level narrative covering organisational structure, business activities, intangibles, financing and relevant tax positions. We coordinate information requests and review consistency with entity-level documentation, subject to the requirements applicable to the group.
subservices.inPractice: We manage the information-gathering across group companies — legal structure charts, value-chain descriptions, intangible ownership and development, intercompany financing arrangements and existing rulings — and edit the contributions into one coherent document. Consistency checks against each Local File remove the contradictions that reviewers look for first.
subservices.youReceive: A group Master File aligned with the entity-level documentation and a reusable information-request pack.

subservices.title: Intercompany agreements
subservices.description: We prepare or review the tax and pricing provisions of agreements for services, goods, funding and other arrangements. The focus includes charging mechanics, allocation keys, payment terms and consistency with actual conduct, with legal review coordinated where required.
subservices.inPractice: We translate the pricing policy into contract language: what is supplied, how the charge is calculated, when true-ups occur, who bears which risks and how the arrangement can be evidenced. Where agreements already exist, we flag clauses that contradict the documented policy or the way the parties actually behave, and propose corrected wording for legal review.
subservices.youReceive: Draft or marked-up agreements with pricing schedules aligned to the documented policy.

subservices.title: Transfer Pricing policy and structuring
subservices.description: We assess proposed operating models and develop pricing policies for distributors, service providers, manufacturers, treasury functions and other group activities. Recommendations consider the allocation of functions and risks, commercial substance and how the policy can be implemented in practice.
subservices.inPractice: A policy is only useful if the finance team can run it. We define the pricing rule for each transaction type, the data inputs it needs, the calculation cadence, who owns monitoring and how new transactions get classified — then test the policy against real numbers before it goes live, so surprises appear on paper rather than in the accounts.
subservices.youReceive: A written pricing policy with calculation templates, monitoring cadence and implementation checklist.

subservices.title: Financial transactions
subservices.description: We analyse intercompany loans, guarantees, cash pooling and extended trade credit. The assessment considers the transaction's nature, borrower circumstances, currency, tenor, security and other relevant terms. A loan benchmark is not automatically suitable for every outstanding trade balance.
subservices.inPractice: The work starts with accurate delineation: is the balance genuinely debt, what are its real terms, and what would independent parties have agreed? We assess the borrower's credit standing, benchmark the interest rate or guarantee fee against market evidence for comparable terms, and document why the chosen reference data fits the transaction under review.
subservices.youReceive: A financial-transactions analysis with credit assessment, rate or fee benchmarking and supporting market evidence.

subservices.title: Management fees and shared services
subservices.description: We review the services performed, recipients' benefits, cost pools and allocation methods. The analysis helps distinguish chargeable services from shareholder or duplicative activities and supports the basis of any markup, with practical documentation of delivery and benefit.
subservices.inPractice: We build the charge from the ground up: which cost centres feed the pool, which activities are excluded as shareholder costs, which allocation keys map cost to benefit, and what evidence shows each recipient actually received something of value. The result is a fee that can be recalculated, invoiced and defended rather than a round number nobody can explain.
subservices.youReceive: A shared-services study with cost-pool definition, allocation model, benefit evidence file and invoicing basis.

subservices.title: Related-party and connected-person remuneration
subservices.description: We assess remuneration and other relevant payments using roles, responsibilities and appropriate market evidence. The analysis considers the full compensation arrangement and relevant legal standard, rather than relying solely on the company's overall profitability to justify a payment.
subservices.inPractice: For payments to owners, directors and other connected persons, we document the role actually performed, gather market reference points appropriate to that role and location, and assess the complete package — salary, benefits, bonuses and other entitlements — against the applicable standard, producing a position the business can apply consistently across years.
subservices.youReceive: A remuneration assessment memorandum with role documentation and market reference analysis.

subservices.title: Disclosure and year-end implementation
subservices.description: We help classify reportable transactions, reconcile disclosure schedules and review actual results against the policy. Where a pricing adjustment is indicated, we assess its basis, accounting treatment and applicable procedural requirements rather than assuming every adjustment is permitted.
subservices.inPractice: At year end we compare booked results with the policy range, prepare the disclosure workings so every figure reconciles to the ledger, and — where an adjustment appears necessary — set out the mechanics: which entity books it, the documentation it requires, its accounting entries and the procedural conditions that apply before it can be reflected in a return.
subservices.youReceive: Completed disclosure workings, results-versus-policy analysis and an adjustment memorandum where required.

subservices.title: Business restructuring and transaction support
subservices.description: We assess the Transfer Pricing implications of moving functions, assets or risks, changing distribution models or reorganising service arrangements. The work identifies relevant valuation or compensation questions and supports transaction planning, documentation and implementation.
subservices.inPractice: Before the reorganisation happens, we map what is actually moving — people, contracts, customer relationships, intangibles, risk — and assess whether the transfer requires compensation and how the post-change pricing should work. We then document the before-and-after arrangements so the file explains the change instead of leaving an unexplained break in results.
subservices.youReceive: A restructuring analysis covering transferred value, compensation assessment and post-change pricing design.

subservices.title: Transfer Pricing audit and litigation support
subservices.description: We help prepare technical explanations, reconcile data and respond to challenges to pricing methods or comparability. Where matters escalate, we provide economic and documentary support alongside appropriately authorised representatives or legal counsel. No outcome is guaranteed.
subservices.inPractice: When a position is challenged, we rebuild the evidential chain: reconciling the questioned figures, stress-testing the original comparables, preparing alternative or corroborating analyses and drafting technical responses that answer the specific challenge raised. Everything is organised so your authorised representatives or counsel can act on it directly.
subservices.youReceive: Reconciled data packs, technical response drafts and supporting economic analyses for the defence team.

subservices.title: Advance Pricing Agreements and MAP support
subservices.description: We assess whether an available advance pricing agreement or treaty-based Mutual Agreement Procedure may be relevant. Support can include feasibility analysis, information preparation and technical submissions, subject to jurisdiction-specific availability, eligibility and procedural requirements.
subservices.inPractice: We start with a realistic feasibility view — the transactions suited to certainty procedures, the information burden, indicative timelines and the strength of your supporting analysis — and then help assemble the submission: transaction description, proposed method, critical assumptions and the economic evidence a reviewing authority will expect to see.
subservices.youReceive: A feasibility assessment and, where pursued, a complete application or submission support pack.

typicalOutputs: Impact assessment; benchmarking report; Local File; Master File; pricing policy; agreement pricing schedules; disclosure workings; authority-response support.

title: Corporate Tax
eyebrow: UAE FEDERAL CORPORATE TAX & FREE ZONE OPTIMIZATION
shortDescription: UAE tax assessments, computations, returns and ongoing advisory support.
description: Corporate Tax affects reporting, commercial arrangements and decisions about how a business is organised. We support UAE businesses in assessing their position, preparing tax calculations and returns, and maintaining evidence for the treatment adopted — from first registration through to ongoing compliance, reliefs and authority interactions.
heroStatement: Structural precision. Confident corporate tax compliance.
services: Free Zone and Qualifying Free Zone Person analysis
Corporate Tax return preparation and filing support
Corporate Tax health check and pre-audit review

capabilities.title: Qualifying Free Zone Person (QFZP) Advisory
capabilities.description: Auditing revenue streams to distinguish Qualifying Income from Excluded Activities, ensuring full compliance with Cabinet Decision No. 139 of 2023 and Ministerial Decision No. 265 of 2023.

capabilities.title: Tax Grouping & Relief Optimization
capabilities.description: Modeling the financial and legal suitability of establishing a UAE Tax Group under Article 40, enabling intra-group loss offsets and eliminating intra-group transfer pricing requirements.

capabilities.title: Restructuring & Participation Relief
capabilities.description: Advising on mergers, demergers, share exchanges, and asset-for-equity transfers under Articles 27 and 28 to defer taxable gains.

approach.title: Corporate Diagnostic
approach.description: Reviewing chart of accounts, contracts, Free Zone licenses, and ownership charts against the Corporate Tax Law.

approach.title: Tax Position Paper
approach.description: Drafting unequivocal technical position papers covering exemptions, reliefs, and accounting-to-tax reconciliation.

approach.title: Tax Accounting Implementation
approach.description: Configuring ERP systems for deferred tax, taxable income calculation, and non-deductible expense tracking.

approach.title: Filing & Defense
approach.description: Preparing statutory corporate tax declarations and handling FTA technical inquiries.

whyItMatters.headline: Why Corporate Tax Strategy is Urgent

points.title: QFZP 5-Year Disqualification
points.text: A breach of the de minimis threshold taints an entire Free Zone entity's 0% status for the current and subsequent 4 tax periods.

points.title: Audit Period Traps
points.text: Unadjusted related party payments or non-deductible entertainment expenses create immediate disallowances upon audit.

points.title: Opening Balance Optimization
points.text: Correct historical valuation of immovable property and intangible assets provides significant long-term shield.

keyDeliverables: Statutory Corporate Tax Computation & Return Files
lede: Corporate Tax affects reporting, commercial arrangements and decisions about how a business is organised. We support UAE businesses in assessing their position, preparing tax calculations and returns, and maintaining evidence for the treatment adopted — from first registration through to ongoing compliance, reliefs and authority interactions.
overviewDescription: UAE tax assessments, computations, returns and ongoing advisory support.
whenToInvolve: You need clarity on how Corporate Tax applies to your entity, Free Zone status or group structure.
The return deadline is approaching and the computation, adjustments and evidence are not yet organised.
You are restructuring, acquiring or disposing of a business and need the tax consequences before signing.
You want a finance-team process that produces a defensible filing every year, not a scramble.

subservices.title: Corporate Tax impact assessment
subservices.description: We assess the entity's activities, ownership, income and arrangements to identify relevant tax obligations and exposures. The resulting assessment explains priority actions, information requirements and matters requiring further technical analysis before filing or restructuring.
subservices.inPractice: We work through your licences, ownership chain, income streams, related-party dealings and accounting policies to establish how the rules apply to your specific facts — which entities are taxable, what elections or reliefs deserve analysis, where exposures sit and what evidence needs to exist before the first or next filing.
subservices.youReceive: An impact memorandum with an entity-by-entity position, priority actions and an evidence checklist.

subservices.title: Registration and deregistration support
subservices.description: We review the relevant circumstances, help assemble application information and support the appropriate process. We also identify connected compliance actions, such as outstanding returns or record requirements, rather than treating registration changes as an isolated administrative exercise.
subservices.inPractice: We confirm which entities need to register or deregister and when, prepare the supporting information the application requires, and deal with follow-up questions. Where a business is closing or restructuring, we map the final-period obligations — returns, records and settlements — so deregistration does not leave loose ends that resurface later.
subservices.youReceive: A completed application pack and a checklist of connected compliance actions.

subservices.title: Free Zone and Qualifying Free Zone Person analysis
subservices.description: We review income streams, counterparties, activities and the conditions relevant to Free Zone treatment. The analysis addresses qualifying and excluded activities, substance, documentation and potential consequences of non-compliance. A Free Zone licence alone does not establish eligibility.
subservices.inPractice: We break your revenue down line by line — what the activity is, who the counterparty is and where it takes place — and test each stream against the qualifying-income framework. We then assess the substance, records and monitoring you need to preserve the position, and quantify what changes if a condition is failed, so the treatment adopted is a decision rather than an assumption.
subservices.youReceive: A revenue-stream classification, qualifying-status assessment and a condition-monitoring checklist.

subservices.title: Corporate Tax computation
subservices.description: We reconcile the financial results to the tax calculation, assess adjustments and review available reliefs, losses and credits where applicable. Working papers document the assumptions, supporting records and tax treatment adopted for significant items.
subservices.inPractice: Starting from the trial balance and financial statements, we prepare a bridge from accounting profit to taxable income: each adjustment identified, calculated and cross-referenced to its supporting evidence. Judgement areas are written up explicitly so management can see the position taken and the reasoning behind it before anything is filed.
subservices.youReceive: A full computation pack with an accounting-to-tax bridge, adjustment schedules and documented positions.

subservices.title: Corporate Tax return preparation and filing support
subservices.description: We prepare or review return data and supporting schedules, reconcile them to the computation and financial records, and identify outstanding matters for management approval. Filing assistance is provided within the agreed scope and appropriate access authorisation.
subservices.inPractice: We populate or review every return field against the computation, reconcile the disclosed figures to the accounts, resolve exceptions and produce a management summary of the positions and open items requiring sign-off. The final filing pack keeps the return, computation and evidence together so later questions can be answered from one place.
subservices.youReceive: A reconciled return pack with management approval summary and an organised filing archive.

subservices.title: Corporate Tax health check and pre-audit review
subservices.description: We review calculations, prior filings, supporting records and internal processes to identify potential errors or weakly supported positions. Findings are prioritised by significance, with recommendations for remediation and further analysis where necessary. This is not a statutory audit.
subservices.inPractice: We re-perform key parts of prior computations, sample-test adjustments against evidence, and probe the areas a reviewer would probe: related-party balances, relief claims, classification judgements and record completeness. You receive a candid picture of where the filing stands up, where it needs strengthening and what a correction would involve.
subservices.youReceive: A prioritised findings report with exposure assessment and remediation recommendations.

subservices.title: Tax grouping, losses and reliefs
subservices.description: We evaluate the conditions and implications of available grouping arrangements, loss utilisation and reliefs. The review considers ownership, financial reporting, restrictions and continuing requirements, helping management weigh administrative benefits against compliance responsibilities.
subservices.inPractice: We test eligibility against the ownership and reporting conditions, model what grouping or a relief claim actually changes — cash, compliance workload, exposure — and set out the ongoing obligations that come with it. Where losses exist, we track their availability, restrictions and interaction with other positions so nothing usable is silently lost.
subservices.youReceive: An eligibility and implications analysis with a loss-and-relief register and recommendation.

subservices.title: Restructuring and investment decisions
subservices.description: We assess the tax consequences of transfers, disposals, reorganisations and proposed ownership arrangements. The advice considers relevant relief conditions and continuing obligations, and identifies steps that should be addressed before transactions are executed.
subservices.inPractice: For each step of the proposed transaction we identify the tax events it triggers, the reliefs potentially available and the conditions attached to them — including those that continue after completion. The advice arrives as a step plan with the sequence, documentation and elections needed, so tax treatment is secured by design rather than argued afterwards.
subservices.youReceive: A transaction step plan with tax analysis, relief conditions and pre-completion action list.

subservices.title: FTA clarification support
subservices.description: We review a specific area of uncertainty, organise the facts and prepare the technical analysis for an appropriate clarification request. We help distinguish questions requiring interpretation from those that can be resolved through existing published guidance. Authority approval is not promised.
subservices.inPractice: We first test whether published guidance already answers the question — a faster and cheaper route. Where genuine uncertainty remains, we frame the question precisely, assemble the complete factual background and prepare the technical analysis supporting your preferred interpretation, then help respond to any follow-up requests during the process.
subservices.youReceive: A clarification application pack with framed question, facts and technical analysis.

subservices.title: Tax accounting and reporting support
subservices.description: We assist with current and deferred tax workings, relevant accounting disclosures and analysis of significant tax positions. The work is coordinated with the finance team and, where appropriate, the financial statement auditor; it does not constitute an audit opinion.
subservices.inPractice: We prepare or review the current tax charge, deferred tax balances and movement schedules, draft the tax notes for the financial statements and document the analysis behind significant or uncertain positions — in a format your auditor can work through efficiently, reducing the back-and-forth at reporting time.
subservices.youReceive: Current and deferred tax workings, draft disclosures and position papers for the audit file.

subservices.title: Tax governance and ongoing support
subservices.description: We help finance teams establish responsibilities, documentation standards and tax review checkpoints. Ongoing support can include transaction queries, periodic updates and practical training, with the frequency and scope agreed to match the business's needs.
subservices.inPractice: We design the annual tax calendar, assign ownership for each obligation, set the documentation standard each filing must meet and build review checkpoints into the close process. Under an ongoing arrangement, your team gets a direct line for transaction questions as they arise — before entries are booked, not after.
subservices.youReceive: A tax governance framework with calendar, responsibility matrix and documentation standards, plus agreed ongoing access.

subservices.title: FTA audit support and remediation
subservices.description: We help organise records, reconcile return positions and prepare responses to requests during a tax review. Where issues are identified, we assess available corrective steps and coordinate any further dispute or representation support required.
subservices.inPractice: From the first information request, we run the response process: a document index mapped to each question, reconciliations that tie the return to the records, and drafted explanations reviewed for consistency before anything is submitted. If the review surfaces genuine errors, we quantify them and set out the correction options with their consequences.
subservices.youReceive: An organised response file with reconciliations, drafted replies and, where needed, a correction plan.

typicalOutputs: Impact memorandum; Free Zone assessment; tax computation and return pack; health-check findings; clarification submission support; tax process recommendations.

title: International Tax
eyebrow: GLOBAL STRUCTURING, PILLAR TWO & TREATY PLANNING
shortDescription: Tax analysis for cross-border operations, investment and group structures.
description: A cross-border decision can have tax implications in more than one country. We assess how domestic rules, tax treaties and the group's operating arrangements interact, helping businesses understand exposure before entering a market, moving activities or making payments overseas — and coordinate local advice in other jurisdictions where the matter requires it.
services: Tax residence and place of effective management
Treaty eligibility and tax residence certificate support
Foreign tax credits and double-taxation review

capabilities.title: Pillar Two (GloBE Rules) Modeling
capabilities.description: Quantifying Effective Tax Rate (ETR) per jurisdiction for MNE groups with consolidated revenue exceeding EUR 750 million, tracking Transitional CbCR Safe Harbors.

capabilities.title: Double Tax Treaty (DTAA) Advisory
capabilities.description: Leveraging the UAE's network of over 140 comprehensive bilateral tax treaties to minimize withholding taxes on dividends, royalties, and technical service fees.

capabilities.title: Cross-Border Permanent Establishment Defense
capabilities.description: Analyzing dependent agent, fixed place, and construction PE exposures under modern OECD Model conventions.

approach.title: Global Architecture Map
approach.description: Documenting legal ownership, operational headquarters, treasury centers, and IP ownership across all tax jurisdictions.

approach.title: Treaty & GloBE Computation
approach.description: Applying relevant DTAAs, domestic GAAR rules, and Pillar Two calculation formulas.

approach.title: Substance Realignment
approach.description: Establishing tangible economic nexus, local management, and documentation to withstand Principal Purpose Tests.

approach.title: Cross-Border Filing Support
approach.description: Coordinating with overseas tax counsel for synchronized multinational reporting.

points.title: Pillar Two Invalidation
points.text: Zero or 9% UAE tax rates can trigger Top-Up Tax in parent entity jurisdictions unless the UAE implements QDMTT.

points.title: BEPS MLI Enforcement
points.text: Foreign tax authorities actively challenge UAE tax treaty claims using the Principal Purpose Test (PPT).

points.title: Digital & Remote Workforce
points.text: Senior executives working remotely from the UAE can unintentionally trigger a corporate tax nexus for foreign enterprises.

keyDeliverables: Pillar Two Readiness & ETR Impact Study
lede: A cross-border decision can have tax implications in more than one country. We assess how domestic rules, tax treaties and the group's operating arrangements interact, helping businesses understand exposure before entering a market, moving activities or making payments overseas — and coordinate local advice in other jurisdictions where the matter requires it.
overviewDescription: Tax analysis for cross-border operations, investment and group structures.
whenToInvolve: You are entering a new market, opening an overseas presence or investing across borders.
Employees, agents or projects operate in countries where the group has no registered entity.
Cross-border payments — dividends, interest, royalties, fees — are flowing without a documented withholding position.
You are buying, selling or reorganising a business with entities in more than one country.

subservices.title: Market entry and holding structures
subservices.description: We compare relevant tax considerations for a proposed investment or operating presence, including entity form, funding and repatriation. Recommendations reflect commercial objectives and substance requirements, with country-specific advice coordinated where necessary.
subservices.inPractice: We build a side-by-side comparison of the realistic structure options — branch versus subsidiary, holding location, debt versus equity funding, and the route profits will take back to investors — assessed across setup, operation and exit. Each option is tested against the substance you can genuinely maintain, because a structure you cannot staff is a liability, not a plan.
subservices.youReceive: A structure comparison paper with a recommended option and the substance requirements it depends on.

subservices.title: Tax residence and place of effective management
subservices.description: We assess where an entity's management and key decisions take place and how the relevant residence rules may apply. The work reviews governance arrangements and supporting evidence, including potential dual-residence questions; incorporation alone may not settle the analysis.
subservices.inPractice: We examine where board and shareholder decisions are genuinely made — meeting locations, who attends, where the agenda is set and where strategic matters are decided — and map that against the residence tests that matter for your entities. Where practice creates risk, we recommend governance changes and the evidence trail that should exist going forward.
subservices.youReceive: A residence assessment with governance findings, risk analysis and an evidence-maintenance protocol.

subservices.title: Permanent establishment analysis
subservices.description: We review offices, personnel, projects, agents and contracting practices to assess potential taxable presence under relevant domestic rules and treaties. Where exposure is identified, we assess the implications for registration, profit attribution and the way activities are organised.
subservices.inPractice: We collect the operational facts — travel patterns, home-office arrangements, project durations, who negotiates and signs, what stock or equipment sits where — and test them against fixed-place, agency and project thresholds in the relevant rules and treaty. Where a taxable presence likely exists, we quantify the attributable profit and the registration consequences; where it can be legitimately managed, we set out the operational changes required.
subservices.youReceive: A PE risk assessment by country and activity, with attribution analysis and recommended operating protocols.

subservices.title: Withholding tax analysis
subservices.description: We assess cross-border payments such as interest, royalties, service fees and dividends against the relevant source-country rules and treaty provisions. The work considers eligibility, documentation and contractual tax clauses; it does not assume the same treatment in every country.
subservices.inPractice: We take each payment flow and determine its character, the domestic withholding treatment, the treaty rate potentially available and the documentation needed to claim it — residence certificates, beneficial-ownership support, contract wording. The output is a payment matrix your finance team can apply at the moment of remittance, not a theory that arrives after the transfer.
subservices.youReceive: A withholding-tax matrix by payment type and country, with the documentation checklist for each flow.

subservices.title: Treaty eligibility and tax residence certificate support
subservices.description: We review the facts needed to support treaty access and help prepare the relevant residence certificate application information. The assessment considers applicable eligibility and anti-abuse conditions. Obtaining a certificate does not by itself guarantee every treaty benefit.
subservices.inPractice: We assess whether your entity genuinely meets the residence and anti-abuse conditions the treaty imposes — including purpose and substance tests — before any application is made, then assemble the application file and supporting evidence. Where eligibility is doubtful, we say so and explain what would need to change, because a certificate obtained on weak facts creates risk rather than relief.
subservices.youReceive: An eligibility assessment and a complete residence-certificate application file.

subservices.title: Foreign tax credits and double-taxation review
subservices.description: We examine the nature of overseas tax, supporting evidence and relevant relief mechanisms. The analysis identifies whether and how double taxation may be addressed, including limitations, timing differences and any further local-country advice needed.
subservices.inPractice: We verify what the foreign amount actually is — a creditable income tax, a withholding that treaty relief should have reduced, or a cost with no relief route — and then work through the mechanism, limits and evidence for claiming relief. Where over-withholding has occurred, we assess the reclaim route in the source country and coordinate local support to pursue it.
subservices.youReceive: A double-taxation analysis with the relief calculation, evidence file and any reclaim recommendation.

subservices.title: Cross-border restructuring
subservices.description: We assess the implications of reorganising ownership, transferring businesses, relocating functions or changing group funding. The work considers transaction taxes, continuing obligations, treaty issues and interaction with Transfer Pricing rather than examining the structure in isolation.
subservices.inPractice: For each restructuring step we identify the consequences in every affected country — exit charges, transaction taxes, treaty access changes, compliance obligations that survive the change — and sequence the steps so avoidable costs are avoided. The Transfer Pricing consequences of moved functions and assets are handled inside the same plan rather than discovered later.
subservices.youReceive: A multi-jurisdiction step plan with tax consequences per step and a coordinated implementation checklist.

subservices.title: Financing and profit repatriation
subservices.description: We review proposed debt and equity arrangements and routes for returning funds to investors. The assessment considers deductibility, withholding, treaty treatment, commercial terms and relevant anti-avoidance rules, with a documented comparison of practical options.
subservices.inPractice: We model the realistic routes for moving funds — dividends, interest, royalties, capital reductions, loan repayments — with the tax cost, timing, documentation and restrictions of each, and stress-test intended interest deductions against limitation and anti-avoidance rules before the funding is booked. The recommendation shows its assumptions so it can be revisited when facts change.
subservices.youReceive: A funding and repatriation options paper with modelled outcomes and a documented recommendation.

subservices.title: International tax due diligence
subservices.description: We review selected cross-border tax exposures in an acquisition, disposal or investment. Findings identify significant assumptions and information gaps and can inform deal discussions, further specialist work and post-transaction priorities.
subservices.inPractice: Working from the data room and management interviews, we probe the target's cross-border pressure points — permanent establishment exposure, withholding compliance, treaty positions, transfer pricing documentation and open authority matters — and translate findings into deal terms: price adjustments, warranties, indemnities and the fix-list for day one of ownership.
subservices.youReceive: A due-diligence report with quantified findings, deal-protection recommendations and a post-completion action plan.

subservices.title: Pillar Two implications for transactions
subservices.description: We assess how a proposed ownership or operating change may interact with a group's global minimum tax position. Detailed scope assessment, modelling and reporting readiness are provided under Global Tax & Emerging Regulations, avoiding duplicate or inconsistent workstreams.
subservices.inPractice: Before a transaction signs, we check whether it changes the group's minimum-tax picture — bringing entities into scope, moving jurisdictional effective rates, disturbing safe-harbour eligibility or shifting reporting responsibility — so the deal model reflects the real post-tax outcome and the detailed compliance work can be scoped without duplication.
subservices.youReceive: A transaction-level minimum-tax impact note feeding the deal model and the wider compliance workstream.

typicalOutputs: Cross-border tax memorandum; residence or PE assessment; payment tax analysis; structure comparison; due-diligence findings; residence certificate application support.

title: VAT & Indirect Tax
shortDescription: Transaction advice, compliance reviews and support across VAT, customs and excise.
description: Indirect tax treatment depends on the transaction, its supporting documents and how it is recorded. We help businesses review VAT processes and cross-border flows, identify errors and maintain a clearer connection between commercial activity, invoices and returns — across VAT, customs duty and excise obligations.
heroStatement: Flawless transactions. Frictionless indirect tax compliance.
services: VAT impact assessment and transaction advice
GCC indirect tax coordination and training

capabilities.title: Cross-Border & Designated Zone Supply Chains
capabilities.description: Resolving complex place of supply issues for goods stored in Designated Zones, triangular trade, and digital services delivered to non-residents.

capabilities.title: Input Tax Recovery & Partial Exemption
capabilities.description: Designing defensible input tax recovery apportionment methods for financial services, real estate, and mixed-use developers.

capabilities.title: Voluntary Disclosures & Penalty Mitigation
capabilities.description: Auditing historical returns, drafting technical disclosure submissions under Article 8 of the Tax Procedures Law, and requesting administrative penalty waivers.

approach.title: Transaction Discovery
approach.description: Reviewing customer contracts, vendor billing, customs entries, and ERP tax codes.

approach.title: Regulatory Analysis
approach.description: Applying UAE Executive Regulations and published FTA Public Clarifications.

approach.title: Process Rectification
approach.description: Correcting tax invoicing templates, credit note protocols, and standard tax rates.

approach.title: Audit Protection
approach.description: Building evidentiary trails for zero-rated export of services and foreign transport.

whyItMatters.headline: Why Indirect Tax Requires Surgical Oversight

points.title: Compounding Penalties
points.text: Failure to submit a Voluntary Disclosure before an FTA audit notification leads to non-negotiable fixed and percentage-based penalties.

points.title: Export of Services Traps
points.text: Zero-rating under Article 31 is frequently denied by the FTA if the foreign customer has a UAE branch or presence related to the supply.

points.title: Cash Flow Friction
points.text: Unclaimed input tax or delayed refunds negatively impact working capital across capital-intensive operations.

lede: Indirect tax treatment depends on the transaction, its supporting documents and how it is recorded. We help businesses review VAT processes and cross-border flows, identify errors and maintain a clearer connection between commercial activity, invoices and returns — across VAT, customs duty and excise obligations.
overviewDescription: Transaction advice, compliance reviews and support across VAT, customs and excise.
whenToInvolve: Your returns are prepared under time pressure and nobody re-checks classification or reconciles them to the ledger.
You trade across borders, through designated zones or in goods where customs and VAT treatment interact.
Input tax recovery is assumed rather than analysed, or a refund position keeps growing.
An authority query, a system change or an acquisition has exposed gaps in the indirect-tax process.

subservices.title: VAT registration, grouping and deregistration
subservices.description: We assess relevant registration and group circumstances and help prepare application information. The work considers business changes and related compliance obligations, with attention to the records and reconciliations required to support the requested treatment.
subservices.inPractice: We test whether registration, group formation or deregistration is actually the right position on your facts — turnover composition, entity relationships, planned changes — and prepare the application with the evidence the authority expects. Group applications include an honest view of the compliance consequences: one return, but joint responsibility and consolidated reconciliations.
subservices.youReceive: A position assessment and complete application pack with the supporting reconciliations.

subservices.title: VAT impact assessment and transaction advice
subservices.description: We review supplies, contracts and invoicing flows to assess the appropriate treatment. Areas can include place and time of supply, exemptions, zero-rating and reverse charge, assessed against the facts and the rules of the relevant jurisdiction.
subservices.inPractice: For each supply type we answer the operative questions in order — what is supplied, by whom, to whom, where and when — and land on the treatment with the contract and invoicing consequences spelled out. New products, new markets and unusual deals get the same discipline before the first invoice is issued, which is far cheaper than correcting a pattern later.
subservices.youReceive: A treatment memorandum per supply type with invoicing requirements and contract-clause guidance.

subservices.title: VAT return preparation and review
subservices.description: We reconcile return data to accounting records, review classification and identify exceptions requiring attention. Supporting workings provide an explanation of the reported amounts and unresolved items for management approval before submission.
subservices.inPractice: Each period we tie every box of the return to the ledger, run exception checks on tax-code usage, large or unusual entries and manual adjustments, and resolve or escalate what falls out. The workings that accompany the return mean any figure can be explained months later without archaeology.
subservices.youReceive: A reviewed return with box-by-box reconciliations and an exception log signed off by management.

subservices.title: Input tax recovery and apportionment
subservices.description: We review recoverability of input tax, allocation methods and supporting documents. For businesses with mixed activities, we assess the basis used to separate recoverable and non-recoverable amounts and identify whether further review or an application is needed.
subservices.inPractice: We test recovery claims against the use of each cost, verify the documents that support deduction, and — for mixed businesses — examine whether the apportionment method actually reflects how costs are consumed. Where the standard method distorts the outcome, we quantify the difference and assess the case for an alternative approach.
subservices.youReceive: A recovery analysis with documentation findings and, where relevant, an apportionment-method assessment.

subservices.title: VAT health checks and corrections
subservices.description: We examine selected periods, transactions and processes for potential errors or gaps. Findings include a prioritised remediation plan and an assessment of appropriate correction or voluntary disclosure routes, subject to applicable rules and the facts identified.
subservices.inPractice: We sample transactions end to end — contract, invoice, entry, return — across the areas where errors concentrate: cross-border flows, adjustments, exempt-input recovery and rate or code changes. Each finding is quantified across the periods affected and matched to the correct correction route, so remediation is a decision made on numbers.
subservices.youReceive: A quantified findings report with period-by-period exposure and a correction roadmap.

subservices.title: VAT refunds
subservices.description: We assess the basis of a refund claim, prepare reconciliations and organise evidence. Support can include responding to requests for further information. Eligibility, timing and payment remain subject to the relevant rules and the authority's review.
subservices.inPractice: We validate the refund position before it is claimed — the causes of the credit, the completeness of supporting documents, the reconciliation between claim and ledger — and assemble the evidence in the structure a reviewing officer will follow. When information requests arrive, responses are prepared from the same organised file rather than rebuilt under deadline.
subservices.youReceive: A refund claim pack with reconciliations, an indexed evidence file and response support.

subservices.title: Cross-border trade and designated zones
subservices.description: We review import and export documentation, supply chains and the tax treatment of goods or services moving across borders. Designated-zone analysis is transaction-specific; VAT designated-zone treatment is distinct from Corporate Tax Free Zone status.
subservices.inPractice: We follow your physical and contractual flows — who ships what, where title passes, which documents exist at each step — and confirm the treatment and evidence each movement needs: export proof, import declarations, zone transfer records. Where goods move through designated zones, treatment is analysed movement by movement rather than assumed from the address.
subservices.youReceive: A flow-by-flow treatment map with the documentary evidence checklist for each movement type.

subservices.title: Customs advisory
subservices.description: We help assess classification, valuation, origin and relevant duty treatment for import and export arrangements. The work can identify documentation needs and inconsistencies between commercial, customs and Transfer Pricing records, with specialist clearance support coordinated where required.
subservices.inPractice: We review tariff classifications against product specifications, test declared customs values against the pricing actually charged — including the effect of transfer-pricing adjustments on declared values — and check origin claims against supplier evidence. Discrepancies between what customs, finance and the TP file each say are surfaced and fixed before an audit finds them.
subservices.youReceive: A customs review covering classification, valuation and origin, with a consistency reconciliation across records.

subservices.title: Excise tax support
subservices.description: We review whether products and activities fall within the relevant excise framework and help organise registration, records and return information. Product treatment and calculation requirements are assessed against current rules; not every business or product is in scope.
subservices.inPractice: We analyse product specifications and business activities against the excise framework to confirm what is genuinely in scope, then set up the registration, stock records, price lists and return workings the regime requires. For borderline products, we document the analysis supporting the position taken so it can be defended if questioned.
subservices.youReceive: A scope determination with registration support and compliant record and return templates.

subservices.title: VAT clarification and audit assistance
subservices.description: We prepare technical analyses for areas of uncertainty and help organise responses during authority reviews. Where a matter becomes disputed, the work connects with Tax Regulatory & Controversy support and appropriate authorised representation.
subservices.inPractice: For genuine uncertainty, we frame the clarification question and build the supporting analysis; during a review, we manage the response file — reconciliations, document indexes, drafted explanations — and check every submission for internal consistency. If the matter hardens into a dispute, the file is already organised for the escalation process.
subservices.youReceive: A clarification submission or an organised audit-response file, consistent and escalation-ready.

subservices.title: E-invoicing and ERP tax controls
subservices.description: We review invoice fields, tax codes, master data and reconciliations from an indirect-tax perspective. System-wide readiness and implementation coordination are addressed under Global Tax & Emerging Regulations, with technology providers involved as appropriate.
subservices.inPractice: We audit how tax is actually determined inside your system — code logic, customer and supplier master data, invoice field population and the reconciliations between subledgers and returns — and specify the corrections that make the system produce compliant documents by default, so accuracy stops depending on manual intervention.
subservices.youReceive: A tax-controls findings report with a prioritised system-correction specification.

subservices.title: GCC indirect tax coordination and training
subservices.description: We help businesses map obligations arising from regional activity and coordinate country-specific advice or compliance support. Practical training can address the transactions and controls used by the finance team. GCC countries must not be treated as one uniform VAT regime.
subservices.inPractice: For businesses operating regionally, we build an obligations map by country — registrations, filings, invoicing rules and their differences — and coordinate local advisers where country filings require them. Training is built from your own transactions and error history, so the finance team practises on the situations they actually face.
subservices.youReceive: A regional obligations map, coordinated country support and a tailored training programme.

typicalOutputs: VAT treatment memorandum; return workings; recovery analysis; health-check findings; refund pack; customs or excise review; tax-control recommendations.

title: Tax Regulatory & Controversy
eyebrow: DISPUTE DEFENSE, FTA RECONSIDERATION & TDRC ADVOCACY
shortDescription: Technical support for authority enquiries, tax audits and disputes.
description: An authority enquiry requires a clear explanation supported by consistent records. We help businesses assess the issue, organise evidence and prepare technical responses — from first information request through reconsideration and dispute — with specialist legal or authorised representation coordinated when the matter requires it.

capabilities.title: FTA Audit Management & Defense
capabilities.description: Serving as primary liaison during FTA audits, controlling information requests, organizing electronic records, and preventing spontaneous auditor misunderstandings.

capabilities.title: Reconsiderations & TDRC Petitions
capabilities.description: Drafting statutory reconsideration requests and formal complaints to the independent judicial Tax Disputes Resolution Committee.

capabilities.title: Penalty Waivers & Installment Plans
capabilities.description: Negotiating administrative penalty reductions and phased payment arrangements with the FTA under statutory relief mechanisms.

approach.title: Assessment Autopsy
approach.description: Dissecting the FTA's statutory basis, factual assumptions, and procedural validity within strict statutory timeframes.

approach.title: Evidentiary Reconstruction
approach.description: Assembling contemporary commercial contracts, banking records, economic benchmarks, and accounting ledgers.

approach.title: Legal Memorial Drafting
approach.description: Formulating detailed technical arguments citing UAE statutes, Cabinet Decisions, and international treaty law.

approach.title: Tribunal Advocacy
approach.description: Presenting oral and written defense before the TDRC and coordinating with licensed UAE litigation counsel.

points.title: Strict 40-Day Deadlines
points.text: Failing to submit a Reconsideration Request within 40 business days permanently crystallizes the tax liability with no legal recourse.

points.title: Pay-to-Appeal Rules
points.text: Appealing to the TDRC requires fulfilling strict statutory deposit requirements or securing explicit exemption orders.

points.title: Evidence Exclusion
points.text: Evidence not presented during initial administrative stages may be dismissed by judicial courts.

keyDeliverables: TDRC Legal Petition & Evidentiary Exhibit Index
Penalty Waiver Dossier under Cabinet Decision No. 49
lede: An authority enquiry requires a clear explanation supported by consistent records. We help businesses assess the issue, organise evidence and prepare technical responses — from first information request through reconsideration and dispute — with specialist legal or authorised representation coordinated when the matter requires it.
overviewDescription: Technical support for authority enquiries, tax audits and disputes.
whenToInvolve: An information request, audit notification or assessment has arrived and the response clock is running.
You have found an error and need to understand the correction routes and their consequences.
A penalty or decision looks wrong and you want the realistic options assessed before deadlines pass.
A significant position needs a written technical defence prepared before anyone asks for it.

subservices.title: Tax audit readiness
subservices.description: We identify the documents, calculations and explanations needed to support significant tax positions. A readiness review highlights missing evidence and inconsistencies so the business can address them before or during a review.
subservices.inPractice: We run your significant positions through a simulated review: for each one, does the evidence exist, is it retrievable, do the numbers reconcile and does everyone tell the same story? Gaps are fixed while there is still time to fix them, and the resulting defence file means an actual review starts from organisation rather than panic.
subservices.youReceive: A position-by-position readiness assessment with a completed defence file and gap-closure plan.

subservices.title: Authority enquiries and information requests
subservices.description: We help interpret requests, allocate information-gathering responsibilities and prepare responses. The focus is a complete, accurate and consistent submission, with material assumptions and open points identified for management rather than concealed.
subservices.inPractice: We decode exactly what is being asked and why, split the request into owned tasks with deadlines, and quality-check the assembled response for completeness and consistency with prior filings before submission. Where information is genuinely unavailable or an earlier explanation needs adjusting, we address it deliberately rather than leaving it to be discovered.
subservices.youReceive: A managed response process with a tracked request register and a reviewed, consistent submission.

subservices.title: Technical position papers
subservices.description: We assess the relevant facts and legal framework and prepare a reasoned explanation of the position adopted. The paper identifies evidence, counterarguments and uncertainty so management and its representatives can evaluate the matter realistically.
subservices.inPractice: We build the argument the way it will be tested: full factual chronology, the legal framework applied to those facts, the supporting evidence indexed against each claim — and an honest treatment of the counterarguments and remaining uncertainty. A paper that concedes nothing convinces no one; ours are written to be relied on.
subservices.youReceive: A reasoned technical position paper with an indexed evidence annex and candid risk assessment.

subservices.title: Private clarification applications
subservices.description: We help frame a suitable technical question and assemble the factual and interpretative material required for an application. The service addresses the request and follow-up process; it cannot promise a favourable interpretation or ruling.
subservices.inPractice: The framing of the question largely determines the usefulness of the answer, so we invest there first — precise, complete and honest about the facts. We then compile the factual annexes and the interpretative analysis, and manage follow-up questions during the review so the process reaches an answer you can actually apply.
subservices.youReceive: A framed application with complete factual and technical annexes, managed through to response.

subservices.title: Voluntary disclosures and remediation
subservices.description: We assess identified errors, quantify relevant differences and review the available correction route. Support includes preparing workings, documenting the reason for the correction and recommending process changes to reduce recurrence.
subservices.inPractice: We establish the full extent of the error across every affected period and entity — partial disclosure creates its own risks — quantify the differences with workings that survive scrutiny, and prepare the disclosure with a clear account of cause and correction. The engagement closes with the process fix, because repeating the same disclosure twice is avoidable.
subservices.youReceive: Quantified correction workings, a prepared disclosure and a recurrence-prevention recommendation.

subservices.title: Reconsideration and penalty-review support
subservices.description: We review the decision and relevant evidence and help prepare the grounds and supporting material for an available application. Eligibility, procedural conditions and deadlines must be checked for the specific matter; relief is not guaranteed.
subservices.inPractice: We give you a realistic merits view first — where the decision is genuinely challengeable and where it is not — then prepare the application: grounds argued against the specific reasoning of the decision, evidence organised to support each ground, and the procedural conditions and deadlines tracked so form never defeats substance.
subservices.youReceive: A merits assessment and a complete, deadline-tracked application with argued grounds and evidence.

subservices.title: Tax dispute and litigation support
subservices.description: We assist with factual chronologies, technical analyses, economic evidence and reconciliation schedules. For proceedings requiring legal representation, we work alongside appropriately qualified counsel rather than presenting tax advisory support as unrestricted rights of audience.
subservices.inPractice: We produce the technical backbone counsel builds on: the agreed and disputed facts separated, every figure reconciled between filings, correspondence and accounts, economic analyses prepared to evidential standard and technical briefings that put counsel fully inside the tax issues. Weaknesses are identified internally first — the other side will find them anyway.
subservices.youReceive: A litigation support pack: chronology, reconciliations, economic evidence and counsel briefing materials.

subservices.title: Cross-border dispute coordination
subservices.description: We assess how a tax adjustment in one jurisdiction affects the group elsewhere and help prepare the information needed for relevant resolution discussions. Treaty-based procedures require separate eligibility and procedural analysis in the countries concerned.
subservices.inPractice: When one country adjusts, we map the knock-on effects across the group — double taxation created, positions elsewhere contradicted, filings needing amendment — and prepare the consistent information set that any resolution procedure will demand, coordinating the advisers in each jurisdiction so the group argues one coherent case, not several conflicting ones.
subservices.youReceive: A group impact map and a coordinated, consistent information pack for resolution proceedings.

typicalOutputs: Evidence index; technical position paper; response pack; correction workings; reconsideration support; litigation-support schedules.

We help businesses establish what applies, identify gaps and plan implementation — separating current obligations from proposals, and turning regulatory change into a managed project rather than a recurring surprise.
heroStatement: Defensible substance. Ahead of regulatory shifts.
services: Pillar Two and UAE Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax scope assessment
Global minimum tax modelling and safe-harbour assessment
Digital business and evolving tax treatment

capabilities.title: Crypto & Digital Asset Taxation (CARF)

approach.title: Regulatory Perimeter Audit
approach.description: Reviewing commercial registry, offshore entities, bank classifications, and cross-border data flows.

approach.title: Gap & Substance Analysis

approach.title: Filing & Portal Submissions

whyItMatters.headline: Why Transparency Regimes Carry Critical Consequences

points.title: Severe Financial Penalties
points.text: Failure to satisfy Economic Substance tests triggers fines starting at AED 50,000 and escalating to AED 400,000 alongside commercial license suspension.

points.title: Spontaneous Treaty Exchange
points.text: Non-compliance automatically triggers the spontaneous exchange of your confidential corporate information with foreign tax authorities.

points.title: Banking De-Risking
points.text: UAE and international tier-1 commercial banks freeze corporate accounts that lack compliant ESR and CRS disclosures.

keyDeliverables: Annual ESR Ministry of Finance Filing Package
CbCR XML Submission & Data Exchange Check
lede: New tax requirements can change data needs, reporting processes and responsibility across a group. We help businesses establish what applies, identify gaps and plan implementation — separating current obligations from proposals, and turning regulatory change into a managed project rather than a recurring surprise.
overviewDescription: Readiness for new reporting requirements, global minimum tax and digital tax administration.
whenToInvolve: Your group may fall within global minimum tax rules and nobody has confirmed scope or owns the data.
E-invoicing or digital reporting mandates are approaching and system readiness is unknown.
Country-by-Country and group reporting obligations are handled ad hoc, entity by entity.
Regulatory developments reach the business through headlines rather than an assessed action list.

subservices.title: Pillar Two and UAE Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax scope assessment
subservices.description: We review the group's structure, financial information and relevant exclusions to assess potential applicability. The work maps affected entities and identifies the data and specialist analysis needed for the next stage without assuming all multinational businesses are in scope.
subservices.inPractice: We test the group against the applicability thresholds and exclusions using its actual consolidated history, entity by entity, and document the conclusion either way — out of scope with reasons, or in scope with a map of affected entities, the data each will need to produce and the analyses that come next.
subservices.youReceive: A documented scope conclusion with an affected-entity map and next-stage data requirements.

subservices.title: Global minimum tax modelling and safe-harbour assessment
subservices.description: We support jurisdiction-level data collection and calculations under the relevant framework and assess available safe-harbour conditions. The analysis documents assumptions and gaps; simplified measures must not be used without establishing that the applicable conditions are met.
subservices.inPractice: We organise the jurisdiction-level data collection, run the effective-rate and top-up calculations under the framework, and test each jurisdiction against the safe-harbour conditions on evidence rather than optimism. Every assumption and data gap is logged, so the model's reliability is visible and improvable rather than assumed.
subservices.youReceive: Jurisdictional calculations, a safe-harbour eligibility assessment and a documented assumptions register.

subservices.title: Top-up tax reporting readiness
subservices.description: We help identify registration and reporting responsibilities, data owners and review controls. Support can include preparing filing information and coordinating with group tax teams or appointed advisers, subject to the specific obligations and authorised filing arrangements.
subservices.inPractice: We turn the obligation into an operating process: who registers where, which entity files what and when, who owns each data feed, and where review checkpoints sit before submission. Dry runs on prior-period data expose the practical problems while they are still cheap to fix.
subservices.youReceive: A reporting responsibility matrix, filing calendar and tested preparation process.

subservices.title: Country-by-Country Reporting
subservices.description: We assess relevant reporting and notification responsibilities and help reconcile entity and jurisdiction data. The work focuses on consistent classification and a clear audit trail. CbCR is distinct from the Master File and Local File, even where information overlaps.
subservices.inPractice: We confirm which entity carries the reporting obligation and which entities owe notifications, then build the report from reconciled source data with consistent entity classification across periods. Because authorities read CbCR alongside your other filings, we sanity-check the picture it paints against the Master File and Local Files before anything is submitted.
subservices.youReceive: A reconciled CbC report and notification schedule with a documented audit trail.

subservices.title: E-invoicing readiness and implementation coordination
subservices.description: We assess applicable scope, invoice data, business processes and system dependencies. We help prepare a gap assessment, implementation priorities and testing requirements with the client's technology providers.
subservices.inPractice: We establish which of your transactions and documents the mandate covers, compare required data fields against what your systems hold today, and map the process changes — issuance, validation, corrections, archiving. The result is a sequenced implementation plan with test scenarios your technology providers can build and verify against.
subservices.youReceive: A scope and gap assessment with a sequenced implementation and testing plan.

subservices.title: Tax technology and data governance
subservices.description: We review how tax data moves from transactions and ledgers into calculations and returns. Recommendations can cover reconciliations, access, version control and exception reviews.
subservices.inPractice: We trace the data journey behind each filing — source entries, transformations, spreadsheets, manual touches — and identify where errors can enter unnoticed. The recommendations are practical controls: standing reconciliations, locked calculation versions, access rules and exception reports that surface anomalies before they reach a return.
subservices.youReceive: A data-flow map with a prioritised control-improvement plan.

subservices.title: Regulatory monitoring and change assessment
subservices.description: We identify developments relevant to the client's business and assess their implications for processes and transactions. Updates distinguish enacted rules, administrative guidance and proposals, with implementation actions and ownership agreed where change is required.
subservices.inPractice: We filter the regulatory stream down to what touches your business, and for each relevant development we state its status honestly — enacted, guidance or proposal — what it changes for you, what to do about it, who owns the action and by when. Monitoring that does not end in an owned action list is just reading.
subservices.youReceive: Periodic change assessments with an owned, dated action register.

subservices.title: Digital business and evolving tax treatment
subservices.description: We assess tax questions arising from digital services, platforms and other emerging business models. Reviews begin with the actual revenue arrangements and jurisdictions involved; the service does not imply that every new technology creates a separate tax regime.
subservices.inPractice: We start from how the model actually earns — who pays whom, for what, where the users and infrastructure sit — and then apply the existing direct and indirect rules to those flows, identifying where treatment is settled, where it is genuinely uncertain and what position and documentation the business should adopt meanwhile.
subservices.youReceive: A revenue-flow tax analysis with recommended positions and the documentation to support them.

subservices.title: Multi-jurisdiction compliance coordination
subservices.description: We help organise obligations, information requests and review milestones across the countries relevant to an assignment. Coordination with locally appointed advisers can support consistency while recognising that jurisdiction-specific filings and legal advice require appropriate local capability.
subservices.inPractice: We act as the single point that keeps a multi-country programme coherent: one obligations calendar, one information-request pipeline to the group, consistency review of local deliverables against the group position, and escalation when a local issue affects everyone else. Local filings stay with locally qualified advisers; coherence stays with us.
subservices.youReceive: A coordinated compliance calendar, managed information flow and consistency-reviewed deliverables.

typicalOutputs: Applicability assessment; data-gap register; modelling schedules; reporting responsibility matrix; e-invoicing readiness plan; regulatory action tracker.
